verdicts.tldr: an icon alone in a link inside a heading that already holds an earlier unlabeled icon never gets its own add-label hint, so the author fixes the heading and still ships a link with no accessible name
verdicts.details: The first icon's walk of the heading sets c.hintDone = true on every Icon at any depth (ext_icons.go:298), nested link included, but stores the answer only on first (first.hint = !named, :310). The nested icon's own parent loop stops at the link (namedByContent is true for KindLink), then returns at :287-288 with hint still false, never walking the link. The hint does surface after the author labels the first icon, since a labeled icon skips aloneInNamedParent and the nested one then walks its link, so the cost is one extra edit-render cycle. Fix: memoize per named parent rather than per icon, e.g. set hintDone only on icons whose nearest named parent is the walked one, or skip descending into a nested Link/GnoLink in the walk.

verdicts.tldr: a heading made only of a labeled icon has an accessible name and an id but no TOC entry, so readers navigating by the TOC cannot reach it; the PR pins this as intended
verdicts.details: writeNodeText (utils.go:197-208) writes only ast.Text and ast.String, so an Icon contributes nothing and the heading's title is empty; toc.go:91-93 reuses a target whose Title is empty and has no Items, so the next same-level heading overwrites it. TestIconHeadingIDAndToc asserts exactly this, with the message "an icon-only heading has no text, so the TOC drops it, label or not", so it is a chosen tradeoff rather than an accident, and the mechanism matches the finder's claim. Fix: have writeNodeText write an Icon's Label (unescaped as the renderer does), so a labeled icon-only heading gets a TOC title, and update that test's expectation.
